claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes thanks for your help. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'd be happy to help you check if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. 

Since Alex is 17 and not currently in full-time education or approved training, I have one more question:

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the past 20 weeks), or is he registered with a careers service or similar organisation as someone who is not in education, training, or employment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't recently left education and isn't registered with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me explain why:

Child Benefit can generally be claimed for children who are:
- Under 16, **or**
- 16-19 and in full-time non-advanced education or approved training, **or**
- 16 or 17 and have recently left education/training (within a limited period) and are registered with a careers service or similar

Since Alex is 17 and is not currently in education or training, hasn't recently left education, and isn't registered with a careers service, he unfortunately doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'm sorry to share that you're **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Summary for Alex:**
Alex is 17 years old and is not currently in full-time education or approved training. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only continue if they remain in qualifying education or training. Since Alex doesn't meet these conditions, eligibility cannot be established.

**What you could consider:**
If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he enrols in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar courses) or an approved training course—you may be able to claim Child Benefit at that point. You would need to notify HMRC of the change in circumstances.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
